entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MORE LOVE TO THEE by William Howard Doane (1832–1915); words by Elizabeth Payson Prentis (1818–1878).
entries.lyrics: More love to Thee, O Christ; More love to Thee; Hear Thou the pray'r I make On bend-ed knee; This is my ear-nest plea, More love, O Christ, to Thee, More love to Thee; More love to Thee.

entries.title: My Faith Has Found a Resting Place
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune LANDAS by William James Kirkpatrick (1838–1921); words by Eliza E. Hewitt (1851–1920).
entries.lyrics: My faith has found a rest-ing place, Not in de-vice or creed; I trust the ev-er-liv-ing One, His wounds for me shall plead. I need no oth-er ar-gu-ment, I need no oth-er plea_, It is e-nough that Je-sus died, And that He died for me.

entries.title: My Faith Looks Up to Thee
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune OLIVET by Lowell Mason (1792–1872); words by Ray Palmer (1808–1887).
entries.lyrics: My faith looks up to Thee, Thou Lamb of Cal-va-ry, Sa-vior di-vine! Now hear me while I pray, take all my guilt a-way, O let me from this day be whol-ly Thine!

entries.title: My God, and Is Thy Table Spread
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1869, 'Rockingham Old') and the score on Wikipedia's article; the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune ROCKINGHAM by Edward Miller (1735–1807); words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751).
entries.lyrics: My God,_ and is Thy ta-ble spread, And does Thy cup with love_ o’er-flow?_ Thi-ther be all Thy child_-ren led, And let them all its sweet__-ness know.

entries.title: My God, How Wonderful Thou Art
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune WESTMINSTER by James Turle (1802–1882); words by Frederick William Faber (1814–1863).
entries.lyrics: My God, how won-der-ful Thou art, Thy maj-es-ty how bright, How beau-ti-ful Thy mer-cy-seat, In depths of burn-ing light!

entries.title: My Hope Is Built
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MELITA by John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876); words by Edward Mote (1797–1874).
entries.lyrics: My hope is built on no-thing less Than Je-sus' blood and right-eous-ness. I dare not trust the sweet-est frame, But whol-ly trust in Je-sus' Name. On Christ the so-lid Rock I stand, All o-ther ground is sink-ing sand.

entries.title: My Jesus, as Thou Wilt
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune JEWETT by Carl Maria Friedrich Ernst von Weber (1786–1826); words by Benjamin Schmolck (1672–1737); translated by Jane Laurie Borthwick (1813–1897).
entries.lyrics: My Je-sus,_ as Thou_ wilt! Oh, may Thy_ will be mine! In-to Thy_ hand of love I_ would_ my all_ re-sign;_ Through sor-row,_ or through_ joy, con-duct me_ as Thine own, And help me_ still to say, my_ Lord, Thy will be done!

entries.title: My Jesus, I Love Thee
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune GORDON by Adoniram Judson Gordon (1836–1895); words by William Ralph Featherstone (1846–1873).
entries.lyrics: My Je-sus, I love_ Thee, I know Thou art mine; For Thee all the fol_-lies of sin I re-sign; My gra-cious Re-deem-er_, my Sa_-vior art Thou_; If ev-er I loved_ Thee, my Je_-sus, ’tis now.

entries.title: My Savior's Love
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MY SAVIOR by Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1856–1932); words by Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1856–1932).
entries.lyrics: I stand a-mazed in the pres-ence Of Je-sus the Naz-a-rene, And won-der how He could love me, A sin-ner, con-demn'd, un-clean. How mar-vel-ous! how won-der-ful! And my song shall ev-er be: How mar-vel-ous! how won-der-ful! Is my_ Sav-ior's love for me!

entries.title: My Soul, Now Praise Thy Maker
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NUN LOB, MEIN SEEL (From Johannes Kugelmann's Concentus Novi, Augsburg, 1540); words by Johann Graumann (1487–1541); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: My soul, now praise thy ma_-ker! Let all with-in me bless His name Who mak-eth thee par-ta_-ker Of mer-cies more than thou dar'st claim. For-get Him not whose meek_-ness Still bears with all_ thy sin, Who heal-eth all thy weak-ness, Re-news thy life with-in. Whose grace and care are end-less And saved thee through the past; Who leaves no suf-f'rer friend-less, But rights the wronged_ at last.

entries.title: Near the Cross
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune NEAR THE CROSS by William H. Doane (1832–1915); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Je-sus, keep me near the cross, There a pre-cious foun-tain— Free to all, a heal-ing stream— Flows from Cal-v’ry’s moun-tain. In the cross, in the cross, Be my glo-ry ev-er; Till my rap-tured soul shall find Rest be-yond the riv-er.

entries.title: Nearer, My God, to Thee
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Lowell Mason's setting, 1859).
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune BETHANY by Lowell Mason (1792–1872); words by Sarah Flower Adams (1805–1848).
entries.lyrics: Near-er, my God, to Thee, near-er to Thee! E’en though it be a cross that_ rais-eth me, Still all my song shall be, near-er, my God, to Thee, Near-er, my God, to Thee, near_-er to Thee!

entries.title: New Every Morning Is the Love
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune MELCOMBE by Samuel Webbe (1740–1816); words by John Keble (1792–1866).
entries.lyrics: New ev-ery morn-ing is the love Our wak-ening and up-ris-ing prove; Through sleep and dark-ness safe-ly brought, Re-stored to life, and power, and thought.

entries.title: No, Not One!
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NO, NOT ONE by George Crawford Hugg (1848–1907); words by Jr., Johnson Oatman (1856–1922).
entries.lyrics: There's not a friend like the low-ly Je-sus, No, not one! no, not one! None else could heal all our soul's dis-eas-es, No, not one! no, not one! Je-sus knows all a-bout our strug-gles, He will guide till the day is done; There's not a friend like the low-ly Je-sus, No, not one! no, not one!

entries.title: Not Worthy, Lord, to Gather Up the Crumbs
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune EVENTIDE by William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Edward Henry Jr. Bickersteth (1825–1906).
entries.lyrics: Not wor-thy, Lord, to ga-ther up the crumbs With trem-bling hand that from Thy ta-ble fall, A wea-ry, hea-vy la-den sin-ner comes To plead Thy pro-mise and o-bey Thy call.

entries.title: Nothing but the Blood
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune PLAINFIELD by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by Robert Lowry (1826–1899).
entries.lyrics: What can wash a-way my sin? Noth-ing but the blood of Je-sus; What can make me whole a-gain? Noth-ing but the blood of Je-sus. Oh! pre-cious is the flow That makes me white as snow_; No oth-er fount I know, Noth-ing but the blood of Je-sus.

Dumont; tune CHRISTUM WIR SOLLEN LOBEN SCHON (traditional Latin, From Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524); words by Coelius Sedulius (5th century); translated by Martin Luther (1483–1546) and Richard Massie (1800–1887).
entries.lyrics: Now praise we Christ, the Ho-ly One, The spot-less vir-gin Ma-ry's Son, Far as the bless-éd sun doth shine E'en to the world's re-mote__ con-fine

entries.title: Now Sin, with Reign Unbroken
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AU MEINES HERZENS GRUNDE by David Wolder (died 1604); words by Thomas Hansen Kingo (1634–1703); translated by Paul Christian Paulsen (1881–1948).
entries.lyrics: Now sin with reign un_-bro-ken, no more can rule my life, Since God the Word hath_ spo-ken, That wins for me the strife; Bap-tized, re-born by grace I_ am re-deem'd from e-vil, And have re-nounced the de-vil and all his works and ways.

entries.title: Now the Day Is Over
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune MERRIAL by Joseph Barnby (1838–1896); words by Sabine Baring-Gould (1834–1924).
entries.lyrics: Now the day is o-ver, Night is draw-ing_ nigh,_ Shad-ows of the eve-ning Steal a-cross the sky.

entries.title: Now the Light Has Gone Away
entries.tune: MÜDE BIN ICH, GEH ZUR RUH
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune MÜDE BIN ICH, GEH ZUR RUH (From Liederbuch für Kleinkinder-Schulen, 1842); words by Frances Ridley Havergal (1836–1879).
entries.lyrics: Now the light has gone a-way; Fa-ther, lis-ten while I pray, Ask-ing Thee to watch and keep And to send me qui-et sleep.

entries.title: O Come, All Ye Faithful
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Hymnal, Episcopal, 1916); checked against the score on Wikipedia's article.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune ADESTE FIDELES by John Francis Wade (died 1786); words by John Francis Wade (died 1786) and Frederick Oakeley (1802–1880).
entries.lyrics: O come, all ye faith-ful, joy-ful and tri-um-phant, O come ye, O come_ ye to Beth_-le-hem; Come and be-hold Him, born the King of an_-gels: O come, let us a-dore Him, O come, let us a-dore Him, O come, let us a-dore Him,_ Christ_ the Lord.

entries.title: O Come O Come Emmanuel
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune VENI EMMANUEL (traditional French); words by Anonymous; translated by John Mason Neale (1818–1866).
entries.lyrics: O come, O come, Em-man__-u-el, And ran-som cap-tive Is__-ra-el, That mourns in lone-ly e_-xile here Un-til the Son of God__ ap-pear. Re-joice! Re-joice! Em-man__-u-el shall come to thee, O I__-sra-el.

entries.title: O Day of Rest and Gladness
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WOODBIRD (traditional German); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: O day of rest and glad_-ness, o day of joy and light, O balm of care and sad_-ness, most beau-ti-ful, most bright: On thee, the high_ and low-ly, through a-ges joined in tune, Sing ho-ly, ho-ly, h_-oly, to the great God Tri-une.

entries.title: O Father, All Creating
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AURELIA by Samuel Sebastian Wesley (1810–1876); words by John Ellerton (1826–1893).
entries.lyrics: O Fa-ther, all cre-a-ting, Whose wis-dom, love, and pow'r First bound two lives to-ge-ther In E-den's pri-mal hour, To-day to these Thy child-ren Thy ear-liest gifts re-new: A home by Thee made hap-py, A love by Thee kept true.

entries.title: O for a Closer Walk with God
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune CAITHNESS (Scottish Psalter); words by William Cowper (1731–1800).
entries.lyrics: O for a clos-er walk with God, A calm and heaven-ly frame, A light to shine up-on the road That leads me to the Lamb!

entries.title: O for a Thousand Tongues
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AZMON by Carl Gotthelf Gläser (1784–1829); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: O for a thou-sand tongues to sing My great Re-deem-er's praise, The glo-ries of my God and King, The_ tri-umphs of His grace!

entries.title: O God, Our Help in Ages Past
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (The Lutheran Hymnary, 1913); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune ST ANNE by William Croft (1678–1727); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748) and John Wesley (1703–1791).
entries.lyrics: O God, our help in a-ges past, Our hope for years to come, Our shel-ter from the storm-y blast, And our e-ter-nal home.

entries.title: O Grieve Not So, nor So Lament
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ERFURT by Ludwig Herman Ilse (1845–1931); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by Sarah Laurie Findlater (nee Borthwick) (1823–1907).
entries.lyrics: O grieve not so, nor so la-ment, My soul! nor trou-bled sigh, Be-cause some joys to o-thers sent Your Fa-ther may de-ny; Take all as love that seems se-vere There is no want if God is near.

entries.title: O Happy Day
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune HAPPY DAY (Wesleyan Sacred Harp (published by William McDonald)); words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751) and Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: O hap-py day, that fixed my choice On Thee, my Sa-viour and my God! Well may this glow-ing heart re-joice, And tell its rap-tures all a-broad. Hap-py day, hap-py day, When Je-sus washed my sins a-way! He taught me how to watch and pray, And live re-joic-ing ev-ery day: Hap-py day, hap-py day, When Je-sus washed my sins a-way!

entries.title: O Holy, Blessed Trinity
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune O HEILIGE DREIFALTIGKEIT by Nikolaus Hermann (1500–1561); words by Martin Behm (1557–1622); translated by Conrad Herman Louis Schuette (1843–1926).
entries.lyrics: O Ho-ly, Bless-ed Trin-i-ty, Di-vine, Es-sen-tial U-ni-ty, God Fa-ther, Son, and Ho-ly Ghost, Be Thou this day my Guide and Host.

entries.title: O Holy Spirit, Enter in
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WIE SCHÖN LEUCHTET by Phillipp Nicolai (1556–1608); words by Michael Schirmer (1606–1673); translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: O Ho-ly Spir-it, en-ter in, And in our hearts Thy work be-gin Thy Tem-ple deign to make us; Sun of the soul, Thou Light di-vine, A-round and in us bright-ly shine, To joy and glad-ness wake us. That we to Thee Tru-ly liv-ing, To Thee giv-ing Prayer un-ceas-ing May in love be still in-creas-ing.

entries.title: O Jesus, I Have Promised
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ANGEL'S STORY by Arthur Henry Mann (1850–1929); words by John Ernest Bode (1816–1874).
entries.lyrics: O Je-sus, I have prom-ised To serve Thee to the end; Be Thou for-ev-er near me, My Mas-ter and my Friend; I shall not fear the bat-tle If Thou art by my side, Nor wan-der from the path-way If Thou wilt be my Guide.

entries.title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. LOUIS by Lewis Henry Redner (1830–1908); words by Phillips Brooks (1835–1893).
entries.lyrics: O lit-tle town of Beth-le-hem, how still we_ see thee lie! A-bove thy deep and dream-less sleep the si-lent_ stars go by. Yet in thy dark streets shin-eth the ev-er-last-ing Light; The hopes and fears of all the years are met in thee to-night.

entries.title: O Lord, How Shall I Meet Thee
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WIE SOLL ICH DICH EMPFANGE by Johann Crüger (1598–1662); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: O Lord, how shall I meet Thee, How wel-come Thee a-right? All na-tions long to see Thee, My Hope, my heart's De-light! O kin-dle, Lord, most ho-ly, Thy lamp with-in my breast, To do in spir-it low-ly All that may please Thee best.

entries.title: O Lord, I Am Not Worthy
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NON DIGNUS (Traditional); words by From Landshuter Gesangbuch, 1777; translated by Anonymous.
entries.lyrics: O_ Lord, I am not wor-thy That_ Thou should'st come to me, But_ speak the words of com-fort, My spir-it healed shall be.

entries.title: O Lord of Heav'n and Earth and Sea
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ES IST KEIN TAG by Johann David Meyer (1636–1696); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: O Lord of_ Heav'n and_ earth_ and sea, To_ Thee all praise and glo-ry_ be; How_ shall we show our love to Thee, Who_ giv-est all?

entries.title: O Love, How Deep, How Broad, How High
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DEO GRACIAS (traditional English); words by Anonymous; translated by Benjamin Webb (1819–1885).
entries.lyrics: O love, how deep, how broad, how high, How pass_-ing thought_ and_ fan-ta-sy, That God, the Son_ of God, should take Our mor-tal form for mor-tals' sake!

entries.title: O Love That Wilt Not Let Me Go

entries.lyrics: Praise God, from whom all bless-ings flow; Praise Him, all crea-tures here be-low; Praise Him a-bove, ye heav’n-ly host; Praise Fa-ther, Son, and Ho-ly Ghost.

entries.title: Praise Him! Praise Him!
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune JOYFUL SONG by Chester G. Allen (1838–1878); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Praise Him! Praise Him! Je-sus, our bless-ed Re-deem-er! Sing, O earth— His won-der-ful love pro-claim! Hail Him! Hail Him! High-est arch-an-gels in glo-ry; Strength and hon-or give to His ho-ly Name! Like a shep_-herd, Je-sus will guard His chil-dren, In His arms He car-ries them all day long. Praise Him! Praise Him! Tell of His ex-cel-lent great-ness; Praise Him! Praise Him! Ev-er in joy-ful song!

entries.title: Praise My Soul the King of Heaven
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune PRAISE MY SOUL by John Goss (1800–1880); words by Henry F. Lyte (1793–1847).
entries.lyrics: Praise, my soul, the King of hea-ven; To His feet thy tri-bute bring. Ran-somed, healed, re-stored, for-giv-en, Ev-er-more His pra-ises sing: A-lle-lu-ia! A-lle-lu-ia! Praise the ev-er-last-ing King.

entries.title: Praise the Lord, Ye Heavens Adore Him
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune AUSTRIA (HAYDN) by Franz Joseph Haydn (1732–1809); words by Edward Osler (1798–1863).
entries.lyrics: Praise the Lord, ye heav'ns, a-dore_ Him; Praise Him, an-gels in the_ height. Sun and moon, re-joice be-fore_ Him; Praise Him, all ye stars of_ light. Praise the Lord,_ for He hath spo_-ken; Worlds His might-y voice o_-beyed. Laws which ne-ver shall be bro_-ken For their_ gui_-dance_ He hath_ made.

entries.title: Praise to the Lord, the Almighty
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score; every note and rhythm agrees with the score on Wikipedia's article.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune LOBE DEN HERREN (Stralsund Gesangbuch); words by Joachim Neander (1650–1680) and Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878).
entries.lyrics: Praise to the Lord, the Al-might-y, the King of cre-a-tion! O my soul, praise Him, for He is thy health and sal-va-tion! All ye who hear, Now to His tem-ple draw near; Praise Him in glad a-dor-a-tion.

entries.title: Redeemed, How I Love to Proclaim It
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune REDEEMED by William James Kirkpatrick (1838–1921); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Re-deemed, how I love to pro-claim it! Re-deemed by the blood of the Lamb; Re-deemed through His in-fi-nite mer-cy, His child and for-ev-er I am. Re-deemed, re-deemed, Re-deemed by the blood of the Lamb; Re-deemed_, re-deemed_, His child and for-ev-er I am.

entries.title: Rejoice, O Pilgrim Throng

entries.lyrics: Re-joice, O_ pil-grim throng! Re-joice, give_ thanks, and sing; Your fest-al_ ban-ner wave_ on_ high, The cross of Christ your King. Re-joice, re-joice, re-joice, Give_ thanks and sing.

entries.title: Rejoice, the Lord Is King
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune DARWALL by John Darwall (1731–1789); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Re-joice, the Lord is King! Your Lord and King a-dore; Re-joice, give thanks, and sing, And tri-umph ev-er-more; Lift up your heart, lift up your voice; Re-joice, a-gain I say, re-joice!

entries.title: Rescue the Perishing
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune RESCUE THE PERISHING by William Howard Doane (1832–1915); words by Fanny Jane Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Res-cue the per-ish-ing, care for the dy-ing, Snatch them in pi-ty from sin and the grave; Weep o'er the err-ing one, lift up the fall-en, Tell them of Je-sus, the might-y to save. Res-cue the per-ish-ing, care for the dy-ing, Je-sus is mer-ci-ful, Je-sus will save.

entries.title: Revive Us Again
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune REVIVE US AGAIN by John J. Husband (died undefined); words by William P. Mackay (1839–1885).
entries.lyrics: We praise Thee, O God! For the Son of Thy love, For Je-sus Who died, And is now gone a-bove_. Hal-le-lu-jah! Thine the glo-ry. Hal-le-lu-jah! A-men. Hal-le-lu-jah! Thine the glo-ry. Re-vive us a-gain.

entries.title: Ride on! Ride on in Majesty
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune WINCHESTER NEW (From "Musikalisches Handbuch", Hamburg, 1690); words by Henry Hart Milman (1791–1868).
entries.lyrics: Ride on! Ride on in ma-jes-ty! Hark! all the tribes ho-san-na cry; O Sa-vior meek pur-sue Thy road With palms and scat-tered gar-ments strewed.

entries.title: Ring the Bells of Heaven
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune RING THE BELLS by George F. Root (1820–1895); words by William O. Cushing (1823–1902).
entries.lyrics: Ring the bells of heav-en! There is joy to-day, For a soul, re-turn-ing from the wild! See, the Fa-ther meets him out up-on the way, Wel-com-ing His wea-ry, wan-d’ring child. Glo-ry! Glo-ry! How the an-gels sing: Glo-ry! Glo-ry! How the loud harps ring! ’Tis the ran-somed ar-my, like a might-y sea, Peal-ing forth the an-them of the free.

entries.title: Safe in the Arms of Jesus
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune REFUGE by William H. Doane (1832–1915); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Safe in the arms of Je_-sus, Safe on His gen-tle breast; There by His love o’er-shad_-ed, Sweet_-ly my soul shall rest. Hark! ’tis the voice of an-gels Borne in a song to me_, O-ver the fields of glo-ry, O-ver the jas-per sea_. Safe in the arms of Je_-sus, Safe on His gen-tle breast; There by His love o’er-shad_-ed, Sweet_-ly my soul shall rest.

entries.title: Satisfied
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune SATISFIED (HUDSON) by Ralph E. Hudson (1843–1901); words by Clara Tear Williams (1858–1937).
entries.lyrics: All my life I had a long-ing For a drink from some clear spring, That I hoped would quench the burn-ing Of the thirst I felt with-in. Hal-le-lu-jah! I have found Him Whom my soul so long has craved! Je-sus sat-is-fies my long-ings, Through His blood I now am saved.

entries.title: Saved by Grace
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune SAVED BY GRACE by George C. Stebbins (1846–1945); words by Fanny Crosby (1820–1915).
entries.lyrics: Some day the sil-ver cord will break, And I no more as now shall sing; But oh, the joy when I shall wake With-in the pal-ace of the King! And I shall see Him face to face, And tell the sto-ry— Saved by grace; And I shall see Him face to face, And tell the sto-ry— Saved by grace.

entries.title: Savior, Like a Shepherd Lead Us
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune BRADBURY by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Dorothy Ann Thrupp (1779–1847).
entries.lyrics: Sa-vior, like a shep-herd lead_ us,_ much we need Thy ten-der care; In Thy plea-sant pas-tures feed_ us,_ for our use Thy folds pre-pare. Bless-èd Je-sus, bless-èd Je-sus! Thou hast bought us, Thine we are. Bless-èd Je-sus, bless-èd Je-sus! Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

entries.title: Savior When in Dust to Thee
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ABERYSTWYTH (PARRY) by Joseph Parry (1841–1903); words by Robert Grant (1778–1838).
entries.lyrics: Sa-vior,_ when_ in dust to Thee Low we bow th'a-dor_-ing knee, When, re_-pent_-ant, to the skies Scarce we_ lift our weep-ing eyes, O by all the pains and_ woes Suff-ered once for man be_-low, Bend-ing from Thy throne on high, Hear our_ pen_-i-ten-tial cry!

entries.title: Saviour, Again to Thy Dear Name We Raise
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ELLERS by Edward John Hopkins (1818–1901); words by John Ellerton (1826–1893).
entries.lyrics: Sa-viour, a-gain to Thy dear name we raise, With one ac-cord our part-ing hymn of praise; We stand to bless Thee ere our wor-ship cease, Then, low-ly kneel-ing, wait Thy word of peace.

entries.title: See Amid the Winter's Snow
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune HUMILITY by John Goss (1800–1880); words by Edward Caswall (1814–1878).
entries.lyrics: See a-mid the win-ter's snow, Born for us on earth be-low, See, the gen-tle Lamb ap-pears, Pro-mised from e-ter-nal years. Hail that ev-er bles-sèd morn, Hail re-demp-tion's hap-py dawn, Sing through all Jer-u-sa-lem: Christ is born in Beth-le-hem.

entries.title: See, the Lord Ascends in Triumph
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune REX GLORIAE by Henry Thomas Smart (1813–1879); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: See, the Lord as-cends in tri-umph; see the King in_ ro-yal state, Ri-ding on the clouds, His char-iot, To His heav'n-ly pal-ace gate. Hark! the choirs of an-gel voi-ces Joy-ful al_-le-lu-ias sing, And the por-tals high are lift-ed To re-ceive their heav'n-ly King. Ho-ly Ghost, Il-lum-in-a-tor, shed Thy beams up-on_ our eyes, Help us to look up with Ste-phen, and to see be-yond_ the skies, Where the Son of Man in glo-ry Stand-ing is at God's_ right hand, Beck-'ning on His mar-tyr ar-my, suc-cor-ing His faith_-ful band.

entries.title: Shall We Gather at the River?
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune HANSON PLACE by Robert Lowry (1826–1899); words by Robert Lowry (1826–1899).
entries.lyrics: Shall we gath-er at the riv-er, Where bright an-gel feet have trod_, With its crys-tal tide for-ev-er Flow-ing by the_ throne of_ God? Yes, we’ll gath-er at the riv-er, The beau-ti-ful, the beau-ti-ful_ riv-er; Gath-er with the saints_ at the riv-er That flows by the throne of_ God.

entries.title: Showers of Blessing
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune SHOWERS OF BLESSING by James McGranahan (1840–1907); words by Daniel W. Whittle (1840–1901).
entries.lyrics: There shall be show-ers of bless-ing: This is the prom-ise of love; There shall be sea-sons re-fresh-ing, Sent from the Sav-ior a-bove. Show-ers of bless-ing, Show-ers of bless-ing we need: Mer-cy-drops round us are fall-ing, But for the show-ers we plead.

entries.title: Silent Night
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune STILLE NACHT by Franz Xaver Gruber (1787–1863); words by Joseph Mohr (1792–1848) and John Freeman Young (1820–1885).
entries.lyrics: Si-lent night,_ ho-ly night,_ All is calm, all is bright, Round yon vir-gin moth-er and child._ Ho-ly in-fant so ten-der and mild, Sleep in heav-en-ly peace,_ Sleep in heav-en-ly peace._

entries.title: Since Jesus Came into My Heart
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune MCDANIEL by Charles Hutchinson Gabriel (1856–1932); words by Rufus H. McDaniel (1850–1940).
entries.lyrics: What a won-der-ful change in my life has been wrought Since Je-sus came in-to my heart; I have light in my soul for which long I have sought, Since Je-sus came in-to my heart. Since Je-sus came in-to my heart, Since Je-sus came in-to my heart; Floods of joy o’er my soul like the sea bil-lows roll, Since Je-sus came in-to my heart.

entries.title: Sing, O Sing, This Blessed Morn
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune NATIVITY by William Henry Monk (1823–1889); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: Sing, O sing, this bless-ed morn, Un-to us a Child is born, Un-to us a Son is giv'n, God Him-self comes down from Heav'n. Sing, O sing, this bless-ed morn, Je-sus Christ to-day is born.

entries.title: Sing Praise to God Who Reigns Above
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune MIT FREUDEN ZART (Bohemian Brethren's Kirchengesange); words by Johann Jakob Schütz (1640–1690); translated by Frances Elizabeth Cox (1812–1897).
entries.lyrics: Sing praise to God who reigns a-bove, The_ God of all cre_-a-tion, The God of power, the God of love, The_ God of our sal_-va-tion. With heal-ing balm my soul is filled And ev-ery faith-less mur-mur stilled: To God all praise and_ glo-ry.

entries.title: Sing to the Lord of Harvest
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune WIE LIEBLICH IST DER MAIEN by Johann Steurlein (died undefined); words by John Samuel Bewley Monsell (1811–1875).
entries.lyrics: Sing to the Lord_ of_ har-vest, Sing songs of love and praise; With joy-ful hearts_ and_ voi-ces Your al-le-lu-ias raise. By Him the roll-ing_ sea-sons In fruit-ful or_-der_ move; Sing to the Lord_ of_ har-vest, A joy-ous song of love.

entries.title: Softly and Tenderly Jesus Is Calling
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune THOMPSON by Will Lamartine Thompson (1847–1909); words by Will L. Thompson (1847–1909).
entries.lyrics: Soft-ly and ten-der-ly Je-sus is call-ing, Call-ing for you and for me; See, on the por-tals He’s wait-ing and watch-ing, Watch-ing for you and for me. Come home_, come home_, You who are wea-ry, come home__; Ear-nest-ly, ten-der-ly, Je-sus is call-ing, Call-ing, O sin-ner, come home!

entries.title: Soldiers of Christ, Arise
entries.source: Open Hymnal Project ABC score (Appendix to Hymns Ancient and Modern, 1869); the opening agrees with hymnary.org's incipit.
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune DIADEMATA by George Job Elvey (1816–1893); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788).
entries.lyrics: Sol-diers of Christ, a-rise, And put your ar-mour on, Strong in the strength which God sup_-plies Through His e-ter-nal Son. Strong in the Lord of hosts, And in His might-y pow’r, Who in the strength of Je-sus trusts Is more than con-quer-or.

entries.title: Songs of Thankfulness and Praise
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune ST. GEORGE by George Job Elvey (1816–1893); words by Christopher Wordsworth (1807–1885).
entries.lyrics: Songs of thank-ful-ness and praise, Je-sus, Lord, to Thee we raise, Man-i-fest-ed by the star To the sa-ges from a-far; Branch of ro-yal Da-vid's stem In Thy birth at Beth-le-hem; An-thems be to Thee add-ressed, God in man made man-i-fest.

entries.title: Souls of Men! Why Will Ye Scatter
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune IN BABILONE (traditional Dutch); words by Frederick William Faber (1814–1863).
entries.lyrics: Souls of_ men! why will ye_ scat-ter Like a_ crowd of_ fright_-ened_ sheep? Fool-ish_ hearts! why will ye_ wan-der From a_ love so_ true_ and_ deep? Was there_ ev-er kind-er shep-herd Half so_ gen-tle, half so_ sweet,_ As the_ Sa-vior who would_ have us Come and_ ga-ther_ round_ His_ feet?

entries.title: Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune MORNING LIGHT by George J. Webb (died undefined); words by George Duffield Jr. (1818–1888).
entries.lyrics: Stand up, stand up for Je-sus! ye sol-diers of the cross; Lift high His roy-al ban-ner, it must not suf-fer loss: From vic-t’ry un-to vic-t’ry, His ar-my shall He lead_, Till ev-ery foe is van-quished, and Christ is Lord in-deed.

entries.title: Standing on the Promises
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune PROMISES by R. Kelso Carter (1849–1928); words by R. Kelso Carter (1849–1928).
entries.lyrics: Stand-ing on the prom-is-es of Christ my King, Through e-ter-nal a-ges let His prais-es ring, Glo-ry in the high-est, I will shout and sing, Stand-ing on the prom-is-es of God. Stand-ing_, stand-ing_, Stand-ing on the prom-is-es of God my Sa-viour; Stand-ing_, stand-ing_, I’m stand-ing on the prom-is-es of God.

entries.title: Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted
entries.tune: O MEIN JESU, ICH MUSS STERBEN
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune O MEIN JESU, ICH MUSS STERBEN (From Geistliches Volkslied, 1850); words by Thomas Kelly (1769–1855).
entries.lyrics: Strick-en, smitt-en, and a-fflic-ted, See Him dy-ing on the tree! 'Tis the Christ by man re-ject-ed; Yes, my soul, 'tis He, 'tis He! 'Tis the long ex-pec-ted pro-phet, Da-vid's Son, yet Da-vid's Lord; Proofs I see su-ffic-ient of it: 'Tis a true and faith-ful Word.

entries.title: Sun of My Soul, Thou Saviour Dear
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune HURSLEY by Franz Joseph Haydn (ascribed) (1732–1809); words by John Keble (1792–1866).
entries.lyrics: Sun of my soul_! Thou Sa_-viour dear, It is not night_ if Thou_ be near: Oh, may no earth-born cloud a-rise To hide Thee from Thy ser_-vant’s eyes!

entries.title: Sunshine in My Soul
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune SUNSHINE by John R. Sweney (1837–1899); words by Eliza Edmunds Hewitt (1851–1920).
entries.lyrics: There is sun-shine in my soul to-day, More_ glo-ri-ous and bright Than_ glows in an-y earth-ly sky, For Je-sus is my light. Oh, there’s sun-shine, bless_-ed sun-shine, When the peace-ful, hap-py mo-ments roll; When_ Je-sus shows His smil_-ing_ face, There is sun-shine in my soul.

entries.title: Sweet Hour of Prayer
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune SWEET HOUR by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by William W. Walford (1772–1850).
entries.lyrics: Sweet hour of prayer! sweet hour of prayer! That calls me from_ a world of care, And bids me at my Fa-ther’s throne Make all my wants_ and wish-es known. In sea-sons of dis-tress and grief, My soul has of-ten found re-lief, And oft es-caped the temp-ter’s snare, By thy re-turn_, sweet hour of prayer!

entries.title: Take My Life and Let It Be

The Com-fort-er has come, The Com-fort-er has come! The Ho-ly Ghost from heav'n, The Fa-ther's pro-mise giv'n; O spread the ti-dings 'round, Wher-ev-er man is found: The Com-fort-er has come!

In sor-row He's my com-fort, in trou-ble He's my stay; He_ tells me ev-ery care on Him to roll. He's the Li-ly of the Val-ley, the Bright and Morn-ing Star, He's the fair-est of ten thou-sand to my soul.

Are you rea-dy? Are you rea-dy? Are you rea-dy for the judg-ment day? Are you rea-dy? Are you rea-dy? For the judg-ment day?

O come to the Fa-ther, through Je-sus the Son, And give Him the glor-y, great things He hath done!

entries.lyrics: Lord Je-sus, I long to be per-fect-ly whole; I want Thee for-ev-er to live in my soul, Break down ev-'ry i_-dol, cast out ev-'ry foe; Now wash me and I shall be whit-er than snow. Whit-er than snow, yes, whit-er than snow; Now wash me, and I shall be whit-er than snow.

entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune ARMAGEDDON by John Goss (1800–1880); words by Frances Ridley Havergal (1836–1879).
entries.lyrics: Who is on the Lord’s side? Who will serve the King? Who will be His help-ers, oth-er lives to bring? Who will leave the world’s side? Who will face the foe? Who is on the Lord’s side? Who for Him will go? By Thy call of mer-cy, by Thy grace di-vine, We are on the Lord’s side, Sa-viour, we are Thine!

entries.title: Why Should Cross and Trial Grieve Me?
entries.licence: Public domain. The Open Hymnal Project marks this hymn “copyright: public domain” (words, music and setting), and places its own editing, indexes and data files in the public domain.
entries.credit: Melody and words from the Open Hymnal Project (public domain), edited by Brian J. Dumont; tune EBELING by Johann Georg Ebeling (1637–1676); words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676); translated by John Kelly (1833–1890).
entries.lyrics: Why should cross and tri-al grieve me? Christ is near With His cheer; Ne-ver will He leave me. Who can rob me of the hea-ven That God's Son, For my own, To my faith hath gi-ven?

entries.title: Will Your Anchor Hold?
entries.licence: Public domain.
entries.credit: Tune WILL YOUR ANCHOR HOLD by William J. Kirkpatrick (1838–1921); words by Priscilla J. Owens (1829–1907).
entries.lyrics: Will your an-chor hold in the storms of life? When the clouds un-fold their_ wings of strife; When the strong tides lift and the ca-bles strain, Will your an-chor drift,_ or_ firm re-main? We have an an-chor that keeps the soul Stead-fast and sure while the bil-lows roll; Fast-ened to the Rock which can-not move, Ground-ed firm and deep in the Sav-iour’s love!

entries.lyrics: Wilt thou, O man, live hap-pi-ly, And dwell with God e-ter___-nal-ly, The ten com-mand-ments keep, for thus Our God Him-self_ bid-deth us._ Kyr' e-lei-son!

entries.lyrics: With-in the Fa-ther's house The Son hath found His home; And to His tem-ple sud-den-ly The Lord of Life hath come.

entries.lyrics: Sing them o-ver a-gain to me, Won-der-ful words of life_; Let me more of their beau-ty see, Won-der-ful words of life. Words of life and_ beau-ty Teach me faith and_ du-ty; Beau-ti-ful words, won-der-ful words, Won-der-ful words of life__; Beau-ti-ful words, won-der-ful words, Won-der-ful words of life.

entries.credit: Tune WORK SONG by Lowell Mason (1792–1872); words by Anna L. Coghill (1836–1907).
entries.lyrics: Work, for the night is com-ing, Work through the mor-ning hours; Work while the dew is spark-ling, Work ’mid spring-ing flow’rs. Work when the day grows bright_-er, Work in the glow-ing sun; Work, for the night is com-ing, When man’s work is done.

entries.lyrics: Ye ser-vants of God, your Mas-ter pro-claim, And pub-lish a-broad his won_-der-ful name; The name all-vic-to-rious of Je-sus ex-tol, His king-dom is glo-rious and rules o_-ver all.

entries.title: Yield Not to Temptation
entries.licence: Public domain. The Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (ccel.org/cceh) states “This music is in the public domain” and that all its files — sheet music, MIDIs and electronic scores — “are free to use in any manner: download, copy, modify, use, distribute, publish, and perform”.
entries.credit: Tune FORTITUDE (PALMER) by Horatio Richmond Palmer (1834–1907); words by Horatio R. Palmer (1834–1907).
entries.lyrics: Yield not to temp-ta-tion, for yield-ing is sin; Each vict’-ry will help you some oth-er to win; Fight man-ful-ly on-ward, dark pas-sions sub-due; Look ev-er to Je-sus, He will car-ry you through. Ask the Sa-viour to help you, Com-fort, strength-en, and keep you; He is will-ing to aid you, He will car-ry you through.
